body.statement: If \(b\le2\), then \(\operatorname{Fail}(S)=1\) if and only if there is \(\beta=(x,r,e^{\to},e^{\leftrightarrow})\in\mathcal B\) whose two edges lie in \(E^{\mathrm{det}}\cup S\) and for which \(r\) reaches \(Y\) in the directed part of \(G_S[V\setminus X]\).  Under the corrected auxiliary-network projection, \(\mathcal O_{XY}\) is exactly the family \(\{L(P):P\text{ is an induced directed }\sigma\text{-to-}t\text{ path in }T^{\mathrm{proj}}\}\).  The child rule in Definition~\ref{def:width-two-projection} enumerates this family exactly once with polynomial preprocessing, worst-case delay including first output and exhaustion, and polynomial working space.
body.justification: Shpitser (2023, Proposition 1) supplies the original-query hedge equivalence; the theorem specializes its certificates at district size two and validates a complete projection algorithm without the unresolved multiple-root recursion.
body.gap: The original-query criterion in Shpitser (2023, Proposition 1) is not an enumeration result, while directed-path and Steiner enumeration do not suppress the exponential multiplicity of deterministic path witnesses or collisions between bow starts that yield the same uncertain support.
body.consumer: It gives an immediately implementable exact compiler for uncertain envelopes with only pairwise latent-confounding districts.
